newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair flies extra flowers for Valentine's Day.
newsitem.headline: Martinair flies extra flowers for Valentine's Day.

text.p: Dutch cargo and charter carrier Martinair proves that romance is not dead as it flies an extra 200 tonnes of flowers into Europe for Valentine's Day.
A spokesman for the Amsterdam-based carrier, said there is definitely more demand for flowers from the European market this year.

On this Thursday, February 13, the Dutch operator is operating an additional cargo flight from Nairobi to the Netherlands, with a Boeing 747 freighter. This freighter will be mostly full of roses, said the spokesman. Usually, Martinair operates four MD-11 freighters a week from Nairobi to the Netherlands.
As well as this, an extra freighter flight, mainly full of carnations, has already been flown from Bogota in Colombia to London Stansted, on February 8, said the spokesman.
"Each year there is more and more demand for flowers generally, not just for Valentine's Day. The flower market is one of the fastest growing sectors," he added.

The airline has seen more demand from the Russians and it has been flying flowers from Africa and Latin America. Flowers are flown by Martinair into the Netherlands and then flown on or trucked by other operators to Moscow.
